step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts a mobile game backend for Akatsuki. Requests originate from mobile clients, passing through an Application Load Balancer to ECS tasks running backend application logic. ECS interacts with Aurora for persistent player data and ElastiCache for caching. To handle traffic spikes, Auto Scaling triggers CloudWatch Events, which invokes a Lambda function to dynamically update the ECS task count within 2 minutes.

graph.name: Akatsuki Scalable Mobile Game Backend
graph.notes: High-concurrency mobile game backend supporting massive auto-scaling and rapid spike handling.

nodes.name: Mobile Client
nodes.notes: External mobile application sending game API requests.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Runs game server containers to compute application logic.

nodes.name: Auto Scaling
nodes.notes: Scales underlying EC2 instances based on load.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Executes logic to adjust ECS desired task count.

nodes.name: Aurora
nodes.notes: Stores primary relational game and player data.

nodes.name: ElastiCache
nodes.notes: Provides in-memory caching for low latency.

edges.notes: ALB routes API traffic to ECS container tasks.
ECS reads and writes persistent player data to Aurora.
ECS retrieves and updates cached state in ElastiCache.
Auto Scaling EC2 instance launch triggers CloudWatch Events.
Lambda scales out ECS tasks to match EC2 capacity.
